content:
Paula Mendes: Hey all — want to lock MVP semantics today so I can update PM-612 + unblock DES-951. Specifically: pause vs rollback, per-tier defaults, and what we show in Console for “why did this happen”.

Marissa Cole: +1. We need something we can message as a safety rail without scaring folks w/ surprise traffic flips.

Jada Williams: From controller side, current spike branch supports `AUTO_PAUSE` only (no execution path for rollback yet). We can add rollback executor next but I’d like MVP definition to match reality.

Chloe Martin: Console-wise, we can ship UI for events + policy editor even if rollback is gated. But we need clear language and avoid “rollback” labels if it only pauses.

Paula Mendes: Proposal for MVP:
1) Default action on breach = auto-pause rollout at current step.
2) Optional action (behind feature flag) = auto-rollback to last known-good step.
3) A/B rollouts: action = shift traffic back to baseline (functionally rollback) OR pause the experiment.

Paula Mendes: Questions:
- Do we call shifting traffic back “rollback” in Console?
- Should self-serve get rollback at all in MVP?

Sean Gallagher: For SRE signoff: ship pause-first. Rollback is riskier (flapping / bad monitors / partial telemetry). If we do rollback in MVP, it needs guardrails + strict defaults.

Ethan Park: Policy engine can support both actions w/ safe bounds. But if the controller can only pause right now, we should spec the schema so rollback can come later without breaking config.

Benji Okafor: +1. Schema can do `on_breach: PAUSE|ROLLBACK|SHIFT_TO_BASELINE` and we validate per rollout type.

Kenji Nakamura: UI preference: Keep it simple. In policy editor, one dropdown “Auto-mitigation action” with options:
- Pause rollout (recommended)
- Roll back to previous version (advanced)
And show a warning banner if you pick rollback.

Marissa Cole: Re per-tier defaults: I’m leaning
- Self-serve (Hosted API): Pause only by default; rollback hidden behind “Advanced” + maybe admin-only until we gain confidence.
- Dedicated: Pause by default, allow rollback if monitors are “safe” (coverage + freshness) and customer opted-in.
- Private: Pause by default; rollback available but off by default because customers may have their own incident process.

Paula Mendes: That matches what I’ve heard. Need exact language around A/B.

Jada Williams: Rollout types:
- Canary/staged model deploy: rollback = revert traffic step to previous model version (idempotent).
- A/B test: “rollback” is ambiguous; it’s really “shift all traffic to baseline” and mark experiment paused/terminated.
I’d suggest we name it “Shift traffic to baseline” in UI, but internally treat it as rollback action.

Chloe Martin: +1. In Console we can render action label based on rollout type:
- Canary: “Rolled back to vX.Y”
- A/B: “Shifted traffic to baseline”
- Staged: “Paused at 25%”
And in the event detail panel we show the decision + metrics summary.

Felix Schneider: For audit timeline, we can display:
- Event: Auto-mitigation triggered
- Action: Paused / Rolled back / Shifted to baseline
- Reason: “SLO breach: p99 latency burn-rate > threshold (fast window)”
- Links: “View SLO monitor” + “View dashboard”
We’ll also need the “suppressed” state (admin override / incident suppression) but that’s later.

Paula Mendes: Great. Now defaults. Can we align on recommended thresholds by tier? I know SRE has guidance.

Sean Gallagher: Rough defaults we can put in PRD (subject to final SLO doc):
- Signals eligible: p95/p99 latency + error rate. Saturation later.
- Evaluation: dual-window burn rate (fast 5m + slow 30m), require both to breach OR fast to breach for N consecutive evals.
- Minimum sample: don’t act unless >= 200 requests in fast window (self-serve) / >= 100 (dedicated) to avoid low-volume noise.
- Debounce/holdoff: after an action, don’t re-evaluate for 15m.

Sean Gallagher: Per-tier action defaults:
- Self-serve: `on_breach=PAUSE`
- Dedicated: `on_breach=PAUSE` (allow ROLLBACK with opt-in)
- Private: `on_breach=PAUSE` (customer can change)

Sean Gallagher: Also: if monitor is missing/stale -> default should be “no action + emit event + alert” (fail-open) for MVP.

Jada Williams: Controller can implement fail-open w/ explicit outcome: `EVAL_INCONCLUSIVE_MONITOR_STALE` and we emit metrics + audit event. That’ll help tune coverage.

Ethan Park: Policy engine validation can enforce:
- rollback requires `min_sample` + `debounce` present
- thresholds within bounds
- action compatibility with rollout type
- if tier=self-serve, rollback requires feature flag + admin permission

Paula Mendes: Re Console appearance: do we show this in rollout creation wizard, policy editor, or both?

Kenji Nakamura: MVP: policy editor section only (since rollout creation wizard is already crowded). Provide template chips:
- “Conservative (Pause only)” (default)
- “Standard (Pause, stricter thresholds)” (maybe later)
- “Aggressive (Rollback)” (advanced)
But ship only Conservative + an Advanced toggle.

Chloe Martin: Works. We can add a read-only summary on rollout details page: “Auto-mitigation: Enabled (Pause on SLO breach)”. Clicking opens policy details.

Marissa Cole: Make sure copy is explicit: “This does not evaluate model quality. Only latency/error SLOs.” And “Auto-mitigation may be suppressed during incidents or by admins.”

Paula Mendes: Good call. I’ll add that to PRD.

Paula Mendes: Decision check:
1) MVP action = PAUSE (everyone gets this when enabled)
2) ROLLBACK is “advanced” + gated; for A/B it shows as “Shift to baseline”
3) Per-tier default templates: self-serve pause-only; dedicated pause-only; private pause-only
4) Console: timeline event + detail panel with metrics + links; policy editor section with dropdown + warnings

Jada Williams: :thumbsup: from controller.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: as long as we’re not defaulting to rollback, and we log monitor-missing cases loudly.

Benji Okafor: :thumbsup: I’ll align schema with those actions + gating.

Chloe Martin: :thumbsup: I’ll tell Felix + Kenji we’ll need string variants per rollout type.

Felix Schneider: Noted. I’ll draft event detail copy that avoids implying “we saved you” and sticks to facts (metrics, thresholds, policy version).

Paula Mendes: Perfect. I’ll update PM-612 + comment on DES-951 with decisions + copy notes. If anyone objects, please reply here today so we don’t churn.

Marissa Cole: Thanks all. Next we should confirm whether we show “Enabled/Disabled” at service default vs per-rollout override. But ok for MVP to keep it service policy-driven.

Paula Mendes: Yep — will capture as open question + v2 item.
